_note: Catalog cross-checked against NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 (control baselines per NIST SP 800-53B): the 20 control families AC, AT, AU, CA, CM, CP, IA, IR, MA, MP, PE, PL, PM, PS, PT, RA, SA, SC, SI, SR. The catalog grain is family-level by deliberate choice (NIST-001): Rev 5 enumerates ~1000+ individual controls and enhancements (e.g. AC-2, AC-2(1)), most of which a given system never selects; family-level ids cover the v1 need (route a control narrative or finding to the right family) with a small, maintainable vocabulary, and the grammar is reserved to add full control/enhancement ids later without a breaking change. Unlike SOC 2 (CC/A/C/PI/P over criteria) and ISO 27001 (themes over controls), NIST families are themselves the top-level grouping, so the pack carries one closed vocabulary (the family catalog), not two. Paperwork existence/metadata/freshness only; ctxgrd never attests that a control is technically enforced (ADR-071 Context).
edition: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 (control families; baselines per SP 800-53B)
summary: NIST 800-53 control-to-evidence register (NIST80053) over the security base — NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: the 20 control families (AC-SR), family-level grain. Paperwork existence/metadata/freshness only, never implementation adequacy.

namespaces.name: NIST80053
namespaces.comment: NIST 800-53 control-to-evidence register (NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, NIST-001/002/003). Each entry maps one control family (from the closed family catalog, projected into core.allowed-values; grain is family-level by choice, NIST-001) to its implementing evidence — a reused POLICY, an ADR, or an `evidence_link` (an SSP narrative, assessment record, or config export). NIST 800-53 introduces no statutory document namespace of its own; the control-to-evidence mapping is its sole artifact, reusing POLICY/RISK/VULN from the security base. Path-claim with an `id` so an audit or a cross-ref can resolve a control. core.calendar-freshness over `review_date` surfaces a stale control. A `not-applicable` control is out of scope. nist.control-evidence (NIST-002) reuses the shared conditional-evidence machinery: an in-scope control asserting a family with neither a POLICY/ADR cross-ref nor a non-empty `evidence_link` fails.
